change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme colour of group member name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The light-theme argument of `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (the removed line in the diff) to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. The PR body only says the dark branch must use `$secondary`; it does not mention changing the light value. The result is that `.name` (line 522) and the sibling `.title` (line 527, still 50%) now render in the same colour, so the name is no longer distinguished from the title in light themes. The same pairing elsewhere is 30% light / 70% `$secondary` dark, e.g. `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/user.scss:124`. Fix: restore `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` as the light argument and use `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` as the dark argument.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of mobile group member name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same change as desktop: the light argument of `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%, so the name (line 497) matches the `.title` directly below it (line 503, 50%) in light themes. This is not what the PR describes, which only adds the `$secondary` dark branch. Fix: restore the 30% light value and use `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark branch.

findings.title: Mobile `.custom-message-length` light colour changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The light-theme argument for `.custom-message-length` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` (removed line) to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. This makes the hint text dark grey in light themes instead of the light grey it was. The desktop rule for the same selector keeps the original pairing, `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss:94` (70% light / 30% `$secondary` dark), so mobile and desktop now disagree. Fix: restore `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` as the light argument; keep `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` as the dark argument, as desktop does.

findings.title: Mobile `.topic-map h3` light colour changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The light-theme argument for `.topic-map h3` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` (removed line) to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, which makes the heading noticeably lighter in light themes. The dark argument is also 50% (`scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)`), whereas the desktop heading for the same component uses 20% / `$secondary` 80% (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:321`). The PR does not describe this change. Fix: use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, matching desktop.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of `.topic-meta-data h5 a` changed from 30% to 70%
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` (bold link), the light-theme argument changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (removed line 290 in the diff) to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. In light themes the link goes from dark grey to pale grey, which is a visible contrast drop. The PR body describes only the dark-theme branch. Fix: restore `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` as the light argument and keep `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark.

findings.title: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses scale-color($primary) with no dark branch
findings.body: The PR converts every `scale-color($primary, ...)` declaration to a `dark-light-choose` call, but this one (line 115, not in the diff) still reads `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);`. In a dark theme `$primary` is the light text colour, so this badge text is not given the `$secondary`-based dark value that the rest of the file uses (e.g. line 48 and line 55 in the same file). Fix: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. Confidence is medium because I did not run the compiler to confirm the rendered dark-theme colour, but the line is unchanged and the dark-theme branch is missing.

contracts.action: Theme-dependent colour declarations: each changed `scale-color($primary, L)` is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, L), scale-color($secondary, 100-L))`
contracts.before_after: Before: every theme gets `scale-color($primary, L)`. After: `dark-light-choose` returns the first argument (the light value, unchanged L) or the second argument (`scale-color($secondary, 100-L)`), decided once at Sass compile time by comparing brightness($primary) with brightness($secondary).
contracts.visible_effect: In a light theme the colour is the same as before for the declarations where the light argument kept its original L. Six light-theme arguments were also changed (findings in desktop/user.scss, mobile/user.scss, mobile/modal.scss, mobile/topic-post.scss, desktop/topic-post.scss), which the PR does not describe. In a dark theme the colour is now derived from $secondary, except the one site at _topic-list.scss:115 that was not converted.
contracts.failure_mode: The scheme is chosen when the stylesheet is compiled, not per element or at runtime, so there is no state to reuse across remounts, Back navigation or background loads. The only failure is a wrong colour for the chosen scheme, which is what the findings above cover; nothing is lost and no error is raised.

summary: Reviewed the 40 stylesheet files in this part. The PR body says scale-color lightness must use $secondary for dark themes. The diff does add that dark branch throughout, and every light/dark pair I checked uses complementary lightness values. But six declarations also change the light-theme argument, which the PR does not mention. Those regress the light theme in desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182 and desktop/topic-post.scss:291. One site was missed: common/base/_topic-list.scss:115 still uses scale-color($primary) with no dark branch. I read the dark-light-choose definition and the flagged files' relevant sections, and grep-checked the stylesheet tree for unconverted sites. I did not compile the stylesheets (the review is read-only), so the rendered colours are inferred from Sass semantics and the source, not from a build. No docs/adr files exist at this commit, so there is no ADR check.
